name: Retatrutide
important: Reconstitute with bacteriostatic water only. Do not use sodium chloride (saline) bacteriostatic water. The wrong diluent can ruin the entire vial.
bacNote: Works with anywhere from 1 mL to 3 mL of bacteriostatic water. Less water makes a stronger solution with smaller draws; more water dilutes it for larger, easier-to-measure draws. Always bacteriostatic water, never saline.

sections.title: Standard titration (once weekly, subcutaneous)
items: Weeks 1 to 4: 2 mg once weekly
Weeks 5 to 8: 4 mg
Weeks 9 to 12: 6 mg
Weeks 13 to 16: 9 mg
Week 17 onward: 12 mg as the target maintenance dose
Hold each dose for the full 4 weeks before going up

sections.title: If you do not need the full dose
items: Many people get strong results and stop climbing at 6 mg or 8 mg
There is no rule that you have to reach 12 mg
Stay at the lowest dose that is still working for you

dosing: Start at 2 mg. In the trials, people who jumped straight to higher doses had far more nausea (around 60%) than those who started low (around 17%), so the slow ramp is the whole point, not a formality.

The newer Phase 3 schedule (above) ramps 2, 4, 6, 9, 12 mg, each held 4 weeks, for the smoothest climb. The older Phase 2 trial jumped 2, 4, 8, 12 and skipped the 6 and 9 mg steps, which works but trades tolerability for speed.
Working range is roughly 4 mg to 12 mg weekly. 12 mg was the highest dose studied and gave the most weight loss.
Pick one day a week and keep it consistent, since the half-life is about 6 days.
duration: Run it in 4-week blocks while titrating. Full programs run 16 to 24 weeks or longer. Many taper the dose down at the end rather than stopping cold, since stopping abruptly tends to bring weight back.
notes: Inject subcutaneously into the stomach, love handles or thigh, rotating the site each week.
GI effects (nausea, early fullness, occasional constipation) hit most in the first week of a new dose and usually settle.
Keep protein intake high and stay hydrated as appetite drops, to hold onto muscle.
Splitting the weekly dose into two smaller shots smooths out side effects for some people.

name: Tirzepatide
bacNote: With a 30 mg vial, 3 mL of bac water gives a clean 10 mg/mL where every titration step is a round number (2.5 mg is 25 units, 5 mg is 50, 10 mg is 100). Smaller vials take 1 to 2 mL.

sections.title: Standard titration (once weekly, subcutaneous)
items: Weeks 1 to 4: 2.5 mg
Weeks 5 to 8: 5 mg
Then step up by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks as needed: 7.5, 10, 12.5, up to 15 mg max
Recommended maintenance doses are 5, 10, or 15 mg
The 2.5 mg step is a starter dose, not a maintenance dose

sections.title: Stop climbing when it is working
items: If you are losing weight and feel fine at 5 mg or 7.5 mg, stay there
Only go up if progress stalls and you are tolerating the current dose

dosing: Start at 2.5 mg for a full 4 weeks. This dose is for letting your gut adjust, not for weight loss.
Move to 5 mg at week 5. From there, only increase by 2.5 mg at a time, never more often than every 4 weeks.
Maintenance lands at 5, 10, or 15 mg depending on response. Plenty of people hold at 5 or 10 mg long term.
Same day each week. Half-life is about 5 days.
duration: A long-run protocol. Titrate over the first 3 to 5 months, then hold your maintenance dose for as long as it keeps working. Stopping tends to bring weight back, so plan your exit.
notes: Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites weekly.
Nausea and early fullness are the common early effects and ease with slow titration.
Keep protein up and stay hydrated to protect muscle while losing weight.

name: Semaglutide
bacNote: Dosed in small amounts, so a 2 mL fill on a 5 mg vial (2.5 mg/mL) keeps the early micro-doses measurable. Adjust the fill to suit the dose you are running.

sections.title: Standard titration (once weekly, subcutaneous)
items: Weeks 1 to 4: 0.25 mg
Weeks 5 to 8: 0.5 mg
Weeks 9 to 12: 1 mg
Weeks 13 to 16: 1.7 mg
Week 17 onward: 2.4 mg as the target maintenance dose
Hold each step a full 4 weeks

sections.title: If 2.4 mg is too much
items: 1.7 mg is a recognised fallback maintenance dose
If nausea at 2.4 mg does not settle after a few weeks, dropping back to 1.7 mg is normal and still effective

dosing: Start at 0.25 mg for 4 weeks. This is a tolerance-building dose and is not expected to do much for weight on its own.
Step up every 4 weeks: 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.7, 2.4 mg, reaching target around week 16.
2.4 mg is the standard maintenance dose for weight, with 1.7 mg as a fallback if 2.4 is not tolerated.
Same day each week. Half-life is about 7 days, so timing is forgiving.
duration: Long-run protocol. Titrate over the first ~16 weeks, then maintain. Stopping commonly leads to weight regain, so plan an exit (taper or maintenance dose) with that in mind.
notes: Inject subcutaneously, rotating sites.
Nausea is the most reported early effect and a smaller starting dose helps.
Protein and hydration matter as appetite falls.

name: Mazdutide

sections.title: Standard titration (once weekly, subcutaneous)
items: Weeks 1 to 4: 1.5 mg
Weeks 5 to 8: 3 mg
Weeks 9 to 12: 4.5 mg
Week 13 onward: 6 mg as the maintenance dose
(A simpler 2 mg, then 4 mg, then 6 mg version on the same 4-week steps is also used.)

sections.title: Watch fasting glucose early
items: Because of the glucagon side of this drug, a small temporary rise in fasting blood sugar in the first 1 to 2 weeks is normal and usually settles by week 3 to 4
A persistent rise means slow the titration down

dosing: Start at 1.5 mg and step up every 4 weeks. Going too fast is the top reason people quit, almost always from nausea.
Maintenance is commonly 6 mg weekly. China approved it at 4 mg and 6 mg in 2025 (brand name Xinermei), and a higher 9 mg dose (titrated 3, 6, 9) is under review there for severe obesity.
Some step down to 4.5 mg or 3 mg once at goal to hold results with fewer side effects.
One consistent day per week. Half-life is about 6.5 days.
duration: Titrate over 12 to 16 weeks, then maintain. Like the other GLP-1 class drugs, stopping tends to bring weight back.
notes: A GLP-1 / glucagon dual agonist, so appetite suppression plus a metabolic bump are the headline effects.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.
GI effects are dose-related and ease with slow titration.

name: Survodutide

sections.title: Standard titration (once weekly, subcutaneous)
items: Start at 0.3 mg once weekly and step up roughly every 2 to 4 weeks toward a working dose, climbing over 14 to 16 weeks
The Phase 2 obesity trial topped out at 4.8 mg weekly
Effects become noticeably stronger from 1.8 mg upward

sections.title: Where most people land
items: 1.8 mg to 4.8 mg weekly is the working range
Do not skip steps; the glucagon and GLP-1 combination makes a fast ramp rough on the gut

dosing: Start at 0.3 mg. This is a tolerance dose; real weight effect kicks in around 1.8 mg.
Step up gradually over 14 to 16 weeks. Steady-state at any dose takes about 5 weeks given the 7-day half-life.
Phase 2 went up to 4.8 mg weekly. Stay at the lowest dose that keeps you progressing.
One consistent day per week.
duration: Titrate over roughly 4 months, then maintain. A plateau after 12 to 16 weeks at your target dose is normal, not failure.
notes: A GLP-1 / glucagon dual agonist studied heavily for weight and metabolic effects.
Inject subcutaneously, rotate sites.
Nausea and fullness early on, easing as the body adjusts.

name: Cagrilintide

sections.title: Standard titration (once weekly, subcutaneous)
items: Mirrors semaglutide: weeks 1 to 4 0.25 mg, weeks 5 to 8 0.5 mg, weeks 9 to 12 1.0 mg, weeks 13 to 16 1.7 mg, then 2.4 mg as maintenance
Hold each step 4 weeks

sections.title: Commonly stacked
items: Cagrilintide is an amylin analogue and is often paired with semaglutide, since the two work by different mechanisms and the combination outperforms either alone
When stacking, titrate each on its own schedule, same day, different injection sites

dosing: Start at 0.25 mg weekly and step up every 4 weeks to 2.4 mg, the same shape as semaglutide.
Trials have gone as high as 4.5 mg weekly, but 2.4 mg is the common maintenance target.
Often run alongside semaglutide for greater effect than either alone.
One day per week. Long-acting, so timing is forgiving.
duration: Titrate over ~16 weeks, then maintain. Some reduce to 1.8 to 2.0 mg weekly once at goal to hold results.
notes: An amylin analogue, so it works on satiety differently than the GLP-1 drugs and stacks well with them.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.
Nausea is the usual early effect.

name: GHK-Cu
bacNote: GHK-Cu is naturally acidic and can sting going in. Filling to the full 3 mL dilutes it as much as the vial allows, which noticeably reduces the burn, so the larger fill is usually preferred. Some co-mix it with BPC-157 to buffer the sting further.
recon: The finished solution will have a faint blue tint. That is the copper and is completely normal.
Once fully mixed it should be clear, not cloudy.

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 1 mg to 2 mg per day, once daily or split morning and evening
At a 3 mL fill on the 50 mg vial (about 16.7 mg/mL), 1 mg is a 0.06 mL draw (6 units) and 2 mg is 0.12 mL (12 units)
The 100 mg vial at 3 mL is twice as concentrated, so halve those draws
A 5 days on, 2 off pattern is common

sections.title: Be patient and inject slowly
items: GHK-Cu works through gene expression, so visible skin and hair changes take weeks
Commit to a 30-day cycle (then 14 days off), ideally 8 to 12 weeks total, before judging it
It is acidic and can sting, so dilute more and push slowly

dosing: Injectable use commonly lands around 1 mg to 2 mg per day.
A 5 days on, 2 days off pattern is popular.
Many run a topical version alongside for skin and hair.
duration: Run in 30-day blocks, then take a short break before the next round.
notes: Copper peptides sting because the solution is acidic. More bac water and a slow push both help.
Popular for skin firmness, fine lines, wound healing and hair quality.
Do not mix in the same syringe as other peptides unless you mean to, since copper can react. BPC-157 is the common deliberate exception.
Inject into a well-rotated subcutaneous site.
storage: A faint blue tint is normal for copper peptides. That colour is the copper itself, not degradation.

name: GLOW
bacNote: GLOW is a blend (GHK-Cu, BPC-157, TB-500 in a 5:1:1 ratio), so 70 mg is the combined weight. The vial is usually 3 mL but occasionally ships as 5 mL; use the fill that matches the vial you received. Filling to the top dilutes the GHK-Cu sting as much as the vial allows. The calculator works in total blend mg: since GHK-Cu is 5 of every 7 parts, a 2.5 mg GHK-Cu dose is 3.5 mg of total blend.
recon: Expect a faint blue tint from the copper in the blend. That is normal.
The solution should be clear once mixed, aside from that blue tint.

sections.title: How a blend is dosed
items: Dose GLOW by the amount of GHK-Cu you want; the BPC-157 and TB-500 come along in the 5:1:1 ratio
The common range is 1 mg to 2.5 mg of GHK-Cu per day, with around 2.5 mg typical during loading
At a 3 mL fill the GHK-Cu portion comes to about 16.7 mg/mL, so 1 mg of GHK-Cu is a 0.06 mL draw (6 units) and 2.5 mg is 0.15 mL (15 units)
At 2.5 mg of GHK-Cu you also get about 0.5 mg each of BPC-157 and TB-500
These figures are for the usual 3 mL fill; with a 5 mL vial, recalculate the draws

sections.title: Schedule
items: One subcutaneous injection daily, or 5 days on, 2 days off, rotating sites
Run an 8 to 12 week block, then 4 to 8 weeks off
Many load daily then drop to 3 times weekly for maintenance
Inject slowly to limit the GHK-Cu sting

dosing: Dose by GHK-Cu content: 1 mg to 2.5 mg of GHK-Cu daily, scaling the whole blend with it. Around 2.5 mg is common during loading.
Once daily, subcutaneous, with sites rotated.
Because it contains copper, inject slowly to reduce sting.
duration: Run 8 to 12 weeks, often 5 days on and 2 off (or daily loading then 3 times weekly), then 4 to 8 weeks off and reassess.
notes: Combines the skin and healing peptide GHK-Cu with the soft-tissue repair pair BPC-157 and TB-500.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.
Because of the copper content, inject slowly to limit any sting.
storage: A faint blue tint is normal because of the GHK-Cu in the blend, not a sign of degradation.

name: KLOW
bacNote: KLOW is a blend (GHK-Cu, BPC-157, TB-500, KPV in a 5:1:1:1 ratio), so 80 mg is the combined weight. The vial is usually 3 mL but occasionally ships as 5 mL; use the fill that matches the vial you received. Filling to the top dilutes the GHK-Cu sting as much as the vial allows. The calculator works in total blend mg: since GHK-Cu is 5 of every 8 parts, a 2.5 mg GHK-Cu dose is 4 mg of total blend.
recon: A faint blue tint from the copper is normal.
The solution should otherwise be clear once mixed.

sections.title: How a blend is dosed
items: Like GLOW, dose KLOW by the GHK-Cu amount; the BPC-157, TB-500 and KPV follow in the 5:1:1:1 ratio
The common range is 1 mg to 2.5 mg of GHK-Cu per day, with around 2.5 mg typical during loading
At a 3 mL fill the GHK-Cu portion comes to about 16.7 mg/mL, so 1 mg of GHK-Cu is a 0.06 mL draw (6 units) and 2.5 mg is 0.15 mL (15 units)
These figures are for the usual 3 mL fill; with a 5 mL vial, recalculate the draws

sections.title: Schedule
items: One subcutaneous injection daily, or 5 days on, 2 days off, rotating sites
Run an 8 to 12 week block, then 4 to 8 weeks off
Inject slowly to limit the GHK-Cu sting
KLOW adds KPV, so it leans more anti-inflammatory than GLOW

dosing: Dose by GHK-Cu content, 1 mg to 2.5 mg daily, scaling the rest of the blend with it. Around 2.5 mg is common during loading.
Once daily, subcutaneous, sites rotated.
Inject slowly given the copper content.
duration: Typically run 8 to 12 weeks, often 5 days on and 2 off (or daily loading then 3 times weekly), then 4 to 8 weeks off and reassess.
notes: Adds KPV (an anti-inflammatory tripeptide) to the GLOW base of GHK-Cu, BPC-157 and TB-500.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.
Inject slowly given the copper content.
storage: A faint blue tint is normal because of the GHK-Cu in the blend, not a sign of degradation.

name: BPC-157

sections.title: Standard healing protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 0.5 mg (500 mcg) per day, the most commonly reported effective dose
Many split it into 0.25 mg morning and 0.25 mg evening
For a specific injury, inject near the affected area; for gut or whole-body benefit, any subcutaneous site works

dosing: Standard daily range is 0.25 mg to 0.5 mg. Start at 0.25 mg for the first week or two, then move to 0.5 mg (often split into two shots) if tolerated.
Consistency matters more than a big dose. Daily dosing beats occasional larger doses.
Mild injuries: 2 to 4 weeks. Severe or post-op: 4 to 8 weeks. Do not run past 8 weeks without a break.
Frequently stacked with TB-500 (the healing or Wolverine stack).
duration: Run 4 to 6 weeks for most injuries, up to 8 weeks for severe or post-surgical cases, then take a break before another cycle. Daily, often 5 days on and 2 off.
notes: Frequently stacked with TB-500 for soft tissue, tendon and ligament recovery.
Daily dosing beats sporadic larger doses. Consistency is the main lever.
Generally very well tolerated.

name: TB-500

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: Loading: 2 mg to 2.5 mg twice weekly (spaced 3 to 4 days apart, e.g. Monday and Thursday) for 4 to 6 weeks
Maintenance: 2 mg once weekly after the loading phase

sections.title: Where it goes
items: TB-500 works systemically, so the injection site does not need to be near the injury
Rotate sites
Often run as the partner to BPC-157 in a healing stack

dosing: Loading: about 2 to 2.5 mg twice weekly for 4 to 6 weeks.
Maintenance: about 2 mg once weekly thereafter.
Long half-life, so twice-weekly dosing is fine; site does not matter since it acts systemically.
TB-500 is on the WADA prohibited list and is banned in competitive sport.
duration: Load for 4 to 6 weeks, then weekly maintenance. Common overall cycle is 8 to 12 weeks on, then a break.
notes: The common partner to BPC-157 for recovery stacks.
Well tolerated by most.
Rotate injection sites.

name: BPC-157 + TB-500 blend
bacNote: A 1:1 healing blend of BPC-157 and TB-500 (the Wolverine blend). The vial weight is the combined total, split evenly: the 10 mg vial holds 5 mg of each, the 20 mg vial 10 mg of each. Dose by the total blend amount; both peptides come along in the 1:1 ratio. The 10 mg vial at 2 mL gives 5 mg/mL total, where 1 mg of blend is a 0.2 mL draw (20 units).

sections.title: How a blend is dosed
items: Dose by the total amount of blend; BPC-157 and TB-500 come along evenly in the 1:1 ratio
The common range is 0.5 mg to 2 mg of total blend per day, with 1 mg per day a solid middle
On the 10 mg vial at a 2 mL fill (5 mg/mL total), 1 mg of blend is a 0.2 mL draw (20 units), which delivers 0.5 mg each of BPC-157 and TB-500
On the 20 mg vial at 2 mL (10 mg/mL total), the same 1 mg dose is a 0.1 mL draw (10 units)

sections.title: Schedule and placement
items: One subcutaneous injection daily, rotating sites
BPC-157 works best near the injury, while TB-500 acts systemically, so for a specific injury you can inject close to the area and still get the whole-body benefit
A 5 days on, 2 days off pattern is common

dosing: Dose by total blend: 0.5 mg to 2 mg per day, with 1 mg a common middle. That splits evenly into BPC-157 and TB-500.
Inject once daily, subcutaneously, rotating sites. For a specific injury you can inject near it.
Both BPC-157 and TB-500 are on the WADA prohibited list and are banned in competitive sport.
duration: Run a 6 to 12 week block, then take a break. Acute injuries often respond in 2 to 3 weeks; chronic or post-surgical cases usually take 4 to 8 weeks to show clear progress.
notes: One daily shot covers both peptides, which is simpler than running two separate vials.
Both peptides are water soluble and mix cleanly in bac water. Rotate injection sites.

name: KPV

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 0.5 mg (500 mcg) once daily is the common working dose
Some start at 0.2 mg to gauge response
For gut-focused use it is often run daily through an active flare

dosing: Common daily dose is around 0.2 mg to 0.5 mg, with 0.5 mg the typical working amount.
Once daily subcutaneous is the usual approach.
Often used in shorter courses during an active inflammatory or gut issue rather than continuously.
Community dosing data for KPV is thinner than for BPC-157 or TB-500, so start conservative and assess.
duration: Typically a 2 to 4 week course around an inflammatory issue, then stop or taper. Repeat as needed around flares.
notes: An anti-inflammatory tripeptide, popular for gut inflammation and skin issues.
Generally well tolerated.
Rotate sites.

name: Tesamorelin
bacNote: Reconstitutes with standard bacteriostatic water. Add the water slowly down the wall and roll the vial gently between your palms for about 30 seconds until the powder dissolves. It foams easily, so never shake it. If a stubborn lot will not clear with bac water alone, a known workaround is adding about 0.1 mL of acetic acid first, then topping up with bac water to the target volume. Most vials never need this.
recon: Roll the vial gently between your palms for about 30 seconds. Do not shake, since it foams readily.
A little foaming on mixing is normal. Let it settle for a minute.
Only if it will not fully dissolve in bac water alone: add about 0.1 mL of acetic acid first, swirl until clear, then add bac water to reach your target volume.

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 2 mg once daily, injected at night
This is the studied clinical dose for reducing visceral fat
Inject on an empty stomach to work with your overnight GH release

dosing: Standard dose is 2 mg once daily at night. Some run 1 mg daily as a lighter approach.
Inject on an empty stomach for the cleanest GH pulse.
Visceral fat reduction is gradual, measured over months, not weeks.
Mild water retention or joint achiness can appear early and usually settles.
duration: Run for at least 3 months given how gradually it works. Many keep it going longer while tracking how they look and feel.
notes: A GHRH analogue used mainly for reducing visceral fat.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.
Mild water retention or joint achiness can show up early and usually settles.

name: Sermorelin
bacNote: Sermorelin can leave a small welt at the injection site. Reconstituting with bac water that contains 0.9% sodium chloride (rather than plain) reduces that reaction for some people. Either works.

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 0.2 mg to 0.3 mg once nightly before bed, on an empty stomach, to ride the natural deep-sleep GH pulse
Daily dosing, since the half-life is very short (about 30 minutes)

dosing: Common dose is 0.2 mg to 0.3 mg, once nightly before bed.
Inject on an empty stomach; food blunts the GH pulse.
Short half-life means daily dosing is needed for steady effect.
A brief flush after injecting is common and passes quickly.
duration: Run 8 to 12 weeks, often 5 days on and 2 off, then take a break. Sleep improvements often show up first, within a couple of weeks.
notes: A GHRH analogue that nudges your own GH output rather than replacing it.
A brief flush after injecting is common and passes quickly.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.

name: Ipamorelin
bacNote: Ipamorelin can cause a small welt at the injection site. Bac water containing 0.9% sodium chloride reduces that for some people. Plain bac water is also fine.

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 0.2 mg to 0.3 mg per dose, once or twice daily, on an empty stomach
The classic timing is before bed and/or fasted in the morning
Start at the lower end (0.1 mg) for the first week

dosing: Common dose is 0.2 mg to 0.3 mg per injection, once or twice daily.
Empty stomach, before bed and/or fasted morning. Wait 20 to 30 minutes before eating.
Selective GH release, so it does not raise cortisol or prolactin the way some secretagogues do.
A brief flush after injecting is normal.
duration: Run 8 to 12 weeks, often 5 days on and 2 off, then a break of similar length. Very commonly paired with CJC-1295 in the same syringe.
notes: A selective GH secretagogue, popular paired with CJC-1295.
A brief flush after injecting is normal.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.

name: CJC-1295 (No DAC)

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 0.1 mg (100 mcg) per dose, once or twice daily, on an empty stomach
Because it is short-acting, it is dosed to match pulses: before bed, fasted morning, or post-workout

sections.title: Best paired
items: Almost always run with Ipamorelin at a matching 0.1 to 0.25 mg (100 to 250 mcg), combined in one syringe, since their short half-lives line up and they amplify each other
Run 8 to 12 weeks, 5 on / 2 off

dosing: Common dose is 0.1 mg to 0.2 mg (100 to 200 mcg) per shot, once or twice daily.
Short half-life (under 2 hours), so time it to pulses and keep it consistent.
Empty stomach. Pairs naturally with Ipamorelin in the same syringe.
A brief flush after injecting is common.
duration: Run 8 to 12 weeks, 5 on / 2 off, then a break.
notes: Almost always paired with Ipamorelin, since the two are complementary.
A brief flush after injecting is common.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.

name: CJC-1295 / Ipamorelin Blend
bacNote: The classic GH pairing of CJC-1295 (No DAC) and Ipamorelin in a 1:1 ratio. The 10 mg vial holds 5 mg of each. Doses below are stated per peptide (they always move together); the calculator works in total blend mg, so 0.2 mg of each peptide is 0.4 mg of total blend.

sections.title: Why these two together
items: CJC-1295 (No DAC) tells the pituitary to make growth hormone, while Ipamorelin tells it to release it: two different signals on the same gland
The No DAC version is used because its short half-life lines up with Ipamorelin, which keeps the natural pulsing pattern intact
They are combined in one syringe and one shot

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 0.1 mg of each peptide before bed is the standard starting dose, moving to 0.2 mg of each for most people
On the 10 mg vial (5 mg of each) at a 2 mL fill, 0.1 mg of each is a 0.04 mL draw (4 units) and 0.2 mg of each is 0.08 mL (8 units)
Dose once daily, 5 days on, 2 days off

sections.title: Timing matters
items: Inject before bed, at least 2 hours after your last meal
Food (especially carbs and fat) blunts the GH pulse, and the body releases its own GH overnight, so a fasted bedtime shot lines up with natural timing
A fasted morning or post-workout dose is the other common slot

sections.title: Titration and ceiling
items: Start at 0.1 mg of each and increase by about 0.05 mg every 1 to 2 weeks if you want, up to a common ceiling of 0.3 mg of each per day (0.12 mL / 12 units at the 2 mL fill)
0.1 mg is already a saturating dose for many, so more is not always better

dosing: 0.1 mg of each peptide is the standard start, 0.2 mg of each suits most people, 0.3 mg of each is a common ceiling.
At the 2 mL fill: 0.1 mg of each is 0.04 mL (4 units), 0.2 mg is 0.08 mL (8 units), 0.3 mg is 0.12 mL (12 units).
Inject once daily before bed, fasted (2 hours after eating), 5 days on and 2 off.
Both peptides are short-acting and share one syringe, so the pairing keeps the natural pulsatile GH release.
duration: Run 8 to 12 weeks (extend to 16 if desired), 5 on / 2 off, then a break.
notes: The most common GH peptide pairing.
One daily shot covers both peptides instead of running two separate vials.
A brief flush after injecting is common and harmless. Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.

name: CJC-1295 (With DAC)

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 1 mg to 2 mg once weekly (some split into two doses per week)
The DAC version is long-acting (half-life of days), so it gives a steady GH bump rather than sharp pulses and does not need daily timing

sections.title: Timing
items: Because it is long-acting, empty-stomach timing matters far less than with the No DAC version
Run 8 to 12 weeks, then a break

dosing: Common dose is 1 mg to 2 mg per week, often as one or two shots.
Long-acting, so you get a sustained GH elevation instead of pulses.
Food timing matters much less here than with the short-acting No DAC version.
Mild water retention or tingling can show up early and settles.
duration: Run 8 to 12 weeks, then a break.
notes: The DAC extends the half-life to days, giving a steady GH bump rather than sharp pulses.
Mild water retention or tingling can show up early and settles.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.

name: GHRP-2
bacNote: Standard bacteriostatic water works fine. A few people prefer plain (non-bacteriostatic) saline because the benzyl alcohol in bac water can sting slightly. This is a soft preference: plain saline is fine for a vial used quickly; bac water gives the longer shelf life for a vial used over weeks.

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 0.1 mg (100 mcg) per dose, one to three times daily, on an empty stomach (30 minutes before food)
A common simple approach is 0.1 mg (100 mcg) before bed, optionally adding a fasted morning dose

sections.title: Best paired
items: Often combined with a GHRH like CJC-1295 (No DAC) for a bigger pulse than either alone
Run 8 to 12 weeks, then a break

dosing: Common dose is 0.1 mg to 0.3 mg (100 to 300 mcg) per shot, one to three times daily.
Empty stomach, 30 minutes before eating.
Raises appetite (a ghrelin mimic), which some want and some do not.
A brief flush after injecting is common.
duration: Run 8 to 12 weeks, then a break.
notes: A ghrelin-mimic GH secretagogue. Tends to raise appetite.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.
A brief flush after injecting is common.

name: GHRP-6

sections.title: Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
items: 0.1 mg (100 mcg) per dose, one to three times daily, on an empty stomach (30 minutes before food)
Expect a strong hunger surge shortly after dosing, more so than GHRP-2

sections.title: Best paired
items: Commonly run with a GHRH like CJC-1295 (No DAC)
Run 8 to 12 weeks, then a break
The big appetite boost makes it a favourite for those trying to eat more

dosing: Common dose is 0.1 mg to 0.3 mg (100 to 300 mcg) per shot, one to three times daily.
Empty stomach, 30 minutes before eating.
Strong appetite boost, more pronounced than GHRP-2. Useful if bulking, less so if cutting.
A brief flush after injecting is normal.
duration: Run 8 to 12 weeks, then a break.
notes: A ghrelin-mimic GH secretagogue with a strong appetite-boosting effect, more so than GHRP-2.
Inject subcutaneously and rotate sites.
